readerTitle: Two businesses lose the same customers. Only one shrinks.
caseNote: 가상 사례 (가정용 밀키트 구독, 식당용 근무표 앱, 사무실 청소 업체) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 반복 매출의 성장은 새 고객만이 아니라 기존 고객이 시간이 지나며 더 많이 쓰게 만드는 구조에서도 나온다. 가격이 고객의 성장에 연결되어 있으면 고객을 잃어도 매출이 늘 수 있다.
misconception: 고객을 잃으면 그만큼 매출이 줄어들고, 매출을 늘리려면 새 고객을 데려오는 수밖에 없다.

sources.text: 구독 사업의 표준 지표 개념 (확장 매출, 순매출 유지율 Net Revenue Retention)

factChecks.note: 순매출 유지율 계산에서 신규 고객 매출은 제외한다는 정의를 카드에 명시했습니다. 업계마다 계산 기간·방식이 조금씩 다르므로 특정 기업의 실제 수치는 인용하지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Two businesses lose the same customers. Only one shrinks.
body: A meal box company and a staff scheduling app both start the year earning $10,000 a month from their customers.
Over twelve months, both lose customers worth $1,000 a month. Neither signs a single new customer. By December, one is earning less. The other is earning more.

image.label: Two shops side by side, one bar shrinking, one growing
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 왼쪽은 밀키트 상자가 쌓인 작은 주방, 오른쪽은 노트북 화면에 근무표가 떠 있는 식당 사무실. 각각 위에 매출 막대가 있고, 왼쪽 막대는 살짝 줄고 오른쪽 막대는 살짝 자라는 모습. 실제 브랜드 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Who earns more from these customers in a year?
body: The meal box charges households a fixed $60 a week. The scheduling app charges restaurants $8 per staff member each month.
Same starting revenue, same cancellations, no new customers. Which one earns more from its customers in December?

options.text: Neither. They lost the same customers, so they end up the same
options.feedback: This counts only who leaves. It ignores what the customers who stay do with their bills over the year.

options.text: The meal box, because people eat every day
options.feedback: Frequent use helps keep customers. But a fixed price per box means a loyal customer pays the same in December as in January.

options.text: The app, if the restaurants that stay keep hiring
options.feedback: Right. Its price grows when the customer grows. The next card shows how much that matters.

cards.title: Same losses, opposite years.
body: Both lost $1,000 a month in cancellations. The restaurants that stayed on the app hired staff and opened new locations, adding **$2,000** a month. The meal box customers who stayed kept ordering the same box.

cards.title: Expansion revenue
body: **Expansion revenue** is the extra money existing customers pay you over time, because they buy more, upgrade or add something.
Many subscription businesses track it with one number: *net revenue retention*. Take this month's revenue from last year's customers, divide by what they paid a year ago, and leave new customers out.
The meal box sits at 90%. The app sits at 110%. Above 100%, your customer base grows on its own.

image.label: A bucket leaking at the bottom and filling from inside
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 양동이 하나에 바닥 구멍으로 물이 조금 새고(라벨 "Cancellations"), 양동이 안의 물방울들이 스스로 커지는 모습(라벨 "Expansion"). 옆에 "90%"와 "110%" 두 개의 숫자 배지.

cards.title: Where expansion comes from.
body: Expansion usually arrives in one of three ways:
list: **More units:** more staff, locations, guests or orders
**Upgrades:** a bigger plan or a higher tier
**Add-ons:** something extra next to what they already buy
cards.callout: The strongest version is the first: a price tied to something that grows when the customer succeeds.

cards.title: The meal box can expand too.
body: Expansion isn't a software trick. The meal box could offer a family size when a household grows, or add-ons like breakfast and desserts.
It could also sell office lunches priced per person. Then every new hire at a client office adds to the bill without a new sale.
The question is the same in any business: when my customer gets bigger or happier, does my revenue from them go up?

cards.title: Expansion cuts both ways.
body: A price that grows with the customer also shrinks with them. When restaurants cut staff in a slow season, the app's revenue falls without a single cancellation.
Pushy upsells can backfire. If customers feel squeezed rather than helped, extra revenue today turns into cancellations later.
And strong expansion can hide trouble. A 110% figure can look healthy while you quietly stop winning new customers.

cards.title: Now it's an office cleaning company.
body: You clean 40 offices for a flat $800 a month each. Some clients have doubled in size since signing, but still pay $800.
Which change would build expansion revenue?

options.text: Raise every client's price by 15% next month
options.feedback: You get a one-time bump, but it isn't tied to anything the client gets. Small clients may feel overcharged and leave.

options.text: Price by floor area and visits, and offer add-ons like window or carpet cleaning
options.feedback: Bills now rise as clients grow or want more, and fall fairly when they don't. It takes effort to reprice existing contracts, so phase it in at renewal.

options.text: Offer a discount for signing a two-year contract
options.feedback: This may keep clients longer. But they still pay the same flat fee however much they grow.

cards.title: Let your revenue grow when your customers grow.
body: Keeping customers matters. So does whether each one is worth more next year than this year.
**Try it today:** pick your three longest-standing customers. Compare what they pay now with what they paid when they started. If it's the same, ask what they'd gladly pay more for.
